structured_output.hypothesis: Oceanic islands have fewer native plant species than similar-sized mainland areas, but a much larger share of their native species is endemic.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using native vascular plant checklists with a geological island-type classification, all three must hold. (1) Among oceanic islands (volcanic or atoll origin, never connected to a continent, with at least 20 native species), the median endemic fraction (species endemic to that island or archipelago divided by native species) is at least 0.20. (2) At least 25% of those islands have an endemic fraction of at least 0.50. (3) Compared with mainland regions of similar area (within a factor of 2), the median endemic fraction of oceanic islands is at least 3 times higher, and their median native richness is lower (Mann-Whitney U test, p < 0.01).
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if any one of these holds. The median oceanic-island endemic fraction is below 0.10. Fewer than 10% of oceanic islands have an endemic fraction of at least 0.50. The oceanic-island median is less than 1.5 times the area-matched mainland median. Oceanic islands are not poorer in species than area-matched mainland regions (p >= 0.05).
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'endemic species' means species found nowhere else in the world. I map this to taxa whose whole native range lies inside one island or one archipelago. 'Oceanic islands' means islands of volcanic or coral origin that have never been joined to a continent, as in the GIFT island-type classification (Galápagos, Hawaii, St Helena and similar). 'Number of kinds of inhabitants' means native species richness. I use vascular plants because GIFT has complete checklists for them. This is a modern reinterpretation: Darwin spoke of all inhabitants, but the test covers plants only. 'Extremely large relative to area' is operationalised as the area-matched comparison with the mainland in criterion (3). His explanation, that colonists are especially liable to modification, is not tested. Only the empirical pattern is.

dataset.name: GIFT
dataset.publisher: University of Göttingen (Biodiversity, Macroecology & Biogeography group), Global Inventory of Floras and Traits
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT compiles regional native and endemic vascular plant checklists for islands and mainland regions worldwide. It records area and island geology (oceanic or continental), and it has an R package and API. Fields to use: entity_ID, geo_entity_ref, area, entity_class or island type (geology and origin), native species counts, and endemic_ref or the endemic species list. I would compute the endemic fraction per entity and compare oceanic islands with area-matched mainland regions.
